demo.title: Jezero rim traverse: the shortest line is not the answer

destination.name: Western rim target (demo coordinate, not a gazetteer feature)

narrative: A two-person crew leaves a base at the Jezero crater reference point for a rim target ~25 km away.
The great-circle line looks shortest, but real MOLA elevations show slopes above the 15° scenario limit.
Terrain-aware and resource-conservative routes avoid them with a ~3 km detour and less climbing.
At 60% of the outbound leg a 35% battery capacity loss and 30% speed loss are simulated.
Continuing breaks the modelled reserves; RedReturn recalculates and shows the revised mission (abort and return).

assumptions.name: terrain_time_factor
assumptions.label: Unresolved terrain (travel-time penalty)
assumptions.rationale: DEM resolution is 463 m; sub-kilometre roughness lengthens real routes. Mean-1 lognormal on travel time.

assumptions.name: climb_energy_factor

assumptions.rationale: Ascent measured on a 463 m grid under-represents true ascent on rough terrain.

Why is this route preferable?.answer: resource has the largest limiting margin (14.8% on time) among routes with no slope/data violations that satisfy every modelled constraint. shortest violates: max_slope. terrain is feasible but its limiting margin differs by -1.4 points. science is feasible but its limiting margin differs by -7.4 points.
evidence: shortest: 25.0 km, ascent 871 m, max slope 18.1°, limiting time 8.7%
terrain: 27.9 km, ascent 678 m, max slope 6.9°, limiting time 13.3%
resource: 27.5 km, ascent 640 m, max slope 8.4°, limiting time 14.8%
science: 27.1 km, ascent 716 m, max slope 10.0°, limiting time 7.3%
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.
suggested_experiments: What if battery capacity drops by 25%?
Which assumption contributes the most uncertainty?

What happens if battery capacity drops b.answer: A 25% battery capacity loss at the halfway point: continuing as planned gives limiting margin 3.3% (feasible within the model). Best modelled option: Abort now and return to base → limiting margin 34.1%, feasible within the model.
evidence: Usable battery capacity reduced 25% (45.0 → 33.8 kWh); reserve threshold kept at the original capacity (conservative).
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.
suggested_experiments: How much extra energy would be needed?

How much additional oxygen would the mis.answer: Deterministic plan uses 2.96 kg O₂ (incl. 15% contingency). To keep a 20% reserve the loaded quantity must be ≥ 3.71 kg (you carry 18.0 kg). Under the ASSUMED input spread, the P90 usage is 4.02 kg → ≥ 5.02 kg loaded.
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.

Which assumption contributes the most un.answer: Largest contributors to the limiting margin (swing between the P10 and P90 of each assumed input, others nominal): Travel speed (31.6 pts, model); Unresolved terrain (travel-time penalty) (19.7 pts, measurement); Unplanned delay (h) (6.6 pts, scenario). Fraction of simulated scenarios satisfying modelled constraints: 73.8% under assumed, not measured, distributions.
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.
suggested_experiments: Which assumption should I measure first?

What evidence supports this terrain clas.answer: Terrain evidence for resource: elevations are MOLA 463 m DEM values (int16 m, MOLA areoid). Max along-track slope 8.4°, max local (Horn) slope 9.6°, ascent 640 m, descent 70 m over 27.5 km. 0 of 50 samples are bilinear interpolations. Features smaller than ~926 m are unresolved.
evidence: Source grid spacing is 463 m. Boulders, dunes, small craters, ripples and rover-scale slopes (<~1 km) are NOT resolved; slopes are averaged over ~1.4 km. Terrain-evaluated is not mission-safe.
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.

Which parts of the route lack adequate s.answer: Data gaps on resource: 0 of 50 samples have no elevation. Not available at all in this build: rock/boulder abundance, high-resolution (HiRISE/CTX) terrain, soil bearing strength, local weather/radiation event data. Rover-scale obstacle avoidance is therefore not assessed anywhere along the route.
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.

What changes improve modeled return marg.answer: Current limiting factor: time at 14.8%. Modelled changes ranked by margin gain: Extend the time window by 20% → +13.5 pts (then limited by energy); Raise travel speed by 20% → +12.8 pts (then limited by time); Reduce science time by 50% → +4.2 pts (then limited by time); Carry 20% more oxygen, water and battery → +0.0 pts (then limited by time).
evidence: Extend the time window by 20%: +13.5 pts
Carry 20% more oxygen, water and battery: +0.0 pts
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.

Why can the system not certify this miss.answer: RedReturn cannot certify this mission: (1) terrain is evaluated only at 463 m, so rover-scale hazards are unseen; (2) no rock/hazard dataset is integrated; (3) resource rates and limits are editable assumptions, not vehicle data; (4) Monte Carlo distributions are hypothetical, not validated probabilities; (5) no independent verification or crew/medical analysis exists. 'Feasible within the model' means only that the stated assumptions pass the stated constraints.
uncertainty: Rates, speed derating and limits are assumptions.
